solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: This writer's put out about lively frolic, unrehearsed

indicators.note: something put out is knocked out of shape, so the word before it is rearranged
about means going round, so the jumbled letters wrap the next word

blocks.note: the setter speaking of himself: I am, shortened
taken as written, then jumbled
a romp is a boisterous frolic

explanation.surface: A writer confesses to being thrown off course by a spontaneous bit of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: An impromptu performance is one given on the spur of the moment, without any preparation or practice.

clue.text: Amateur in grip of old pro, substantial?

indicators.note: something held in the grip of another is enclosed by it

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for amateur
a moll is an archaic word for a prostitute

explanation.surface: An amateur falls into the clutches of a seasoned professional, with a hint of something weighty.
explanation.walkthrough: Pro here is short for prostitute, not professional. The question mark flags a stretched definition: molal concentration counts moles, the unit of amount of substance.
explanation.definitionFit: Molal is a chemistry term measuring amount of substance per kilogram of solvent, so it concerns substance in a technical sense.

clue.text: Dad's enveloped by homily as of old, gassy stuff

indicators.note: a thing enveloped is wrapped up entirely inside another

blocks.note: prone is an obsolete word for a homily or sermon
pa is a familiar word for father; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Father gets wrapped up in an old-fashioned sermon, full of hot air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gassy stuff' looks like a jibe at the windy sermon, but it is the literal definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Propane is a hydrocarbon gas used as fuel, so it is literally a gaseous substance.

clue.text: Naiad involving us in a lark, swimming

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other phrase
swimming letters are moving about freely, so they rearrange

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A water nymph drags us into some fun in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusalka is a water sprite of Slavic folklore, the equivalent of a classical naiad or river nymph.

clue.text: Ribs? Huge, emerging from college shortly

indicators.note: what emerges from something leaves it behind, so those letters are stripped away

blocks.note: colossal means enormous
Coll is the short form of college

explanation.surface: Someone's huge ribcage, perhaps, is seen leaving a college.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of COLL are split, COL at the front of colossal and L at its end; removing them leaves the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is the Latin plural for bones, and ribs are an example of bones, hence the question mark.

clue.text: With HM no longer on board, bales ship out? We'll go off rapidly

indicators.note: someone on board is inside the ship, so the royal letters sit within
the cargo is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, was Her Majesty until 2022, so no longer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Cargo is unloaded from a ship once the Queen has left, and it is the kind that spoils fast.
explanation.walkthrough: HM is Her Majesty; since the death of Elizabeth II, ER is no longer the reigning monarch's cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Perishables are goods such as fresh food that decay quickly, so they speak of themselves as going off fast.

clue.text: Old decoy, name separate, inverted

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down entry means the words run bottom to top

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
apart means separate

explanation.surface: An old lure is identified, set aside and turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Trapan is an archaic form of trepan, meaning a snare or one who lures others into a trap.

clue.text: Roman magistrate? See special one in seat

indicators.note: the one inside is what is left once the outer letter is shed

blocks.note: S stands for special, as in SAS, the Special Air Service
a sedile is a seat in a church chancel for the officiating clergy

explanation.surface: A Roman official spots a privileged figure in a seat.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer plus S makes the seat, so the clue is built backwards: find the seat, then take away the special letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An edile, or aedile, was an official of ancient Rome responsible for public buildings, games and the grain supply.

clue.text: Contract top to bottom in frame

indicators.note: the first letter in a down entry is moved from the top down to the foot

blocks.note: a lease is a rental contract

explanation.surface: Someone shrinks a picture from top to bottom inside its frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contract' looks like a verb meaning shrink, but it is the noun, a legal agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is the stand or frame that holds a painter's canvas or a display board.

clue.text: Bile after rest's disturbed – I'll sever friendship

indicators.note: disturbed things are thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged
after places one piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: taken as written; the 's stands for 'is'
bile is bad temper or anger

explanation.surface: A sleep is broken, the victim's temper flares, and they vow to end a friendship.
explanation.definitionFit: An estranger is one who alienates others, someone who breaks off a relationship.

clue.text: Cluster of cells, type wherein time's passed, American

indicators.note: time having passed means it has gone, so its abbreviation is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a sort is a type or kind
T is the abbreviation for time
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: Someone studies a cell cluster of the kind where time has moved on, in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorus is a botanical term for a cluster of spore-producing cases on the underside of a fern frond.

clue.text: Study beyond traditional methods rate limiting compound of arsenic

indicators.note: to limit something is to set bounds around it, so one word encloses the other
a chemical compound recombines its elements, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: pace is a rate of movement
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chemist's unorthodox research slows the rate at which an arsenic compound forms.
explanation.definitionFit: Parascience is investigation of phenomena outside the scope of conventional science, using unorthodox approaches.

clue.text: Coarse Scots ground-bass regularly missed out

indicators.note: missing out at regular intervals means every other letter is skipped

blocks.note: the even letters are kept and the odd ones skipped

explanation.surface: A rough Scottish musician keeps dropping notes from the bass line.
explanation.walkthrough: A ground-bass is a repeated bass melody; take its second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudas is a Scots adjective meaning coarse or rough, often used of a bold, unmannerly woman.

clue.text: Fine wastage?

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil grades
loss is wastage

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: floss silk is the fine, loose silk on the outside of a cocoon, which is waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Floss is the rough outer silk of a silkworm's cocoon, unusable for reeling, so it is fine fibre that gets thrown away.

clue.text: Student of e.g. Saudi culture, one twice engrossed in pictures etc

indicators.note: someone engrossed in a thing is absorbed inside it

blocks.note: a means one
bis is Latin for twice, used in music for a repeat
art covers paintings and the like

explanation.surface: A scholar of Arabia is twice as absorbed in paintings and similar works.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arabist is a scholar of Arabic language, literature and culture, such as that of Saudi Arabia.

clue.text: Rodent fancying sweet bulbs in quantity – once worth trapping it

indicators.note: trapping means catching and holding inside, and it points back to the preceding item

blocks.note: carat once meant worth or value
a mass is a large quantity

explanation.surface: A rodent with a taste for sweet bulbs eats them in bulk, which was once worth catching.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on into 'in quantity'; the break comes after 'bulbs'.
explanation.definitionFit: The camass rat is a North American pocket gopher named after the camass plant whose edible bulbs it eats.

clue.text: One extracting hemp seeds, Jack maybe, bagging pound

indicators.note: bagging means putting something into a bag, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: Jack the Ripper is an example of a ripper
L is the symbol for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: A farm worker stripping seed from hemp, possibly a Jack, pockets a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack maybe' points to the Victorian murderer; 'maybe' marks him as one example of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To ripple flax or hemp is to comb off its seeds, so a rippler is the worker or tool doing that.

clue.text: All confused maid admits being rendered speechless

definitions.note: a gerund phrase standing for the noun

indicators.note: confused things are mixed up, so the letters of the word before are rearranged
to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an aia or ayah is a maid or nurse in India
taken as written

explanation.surface: A completely flustered maid confesses she was struck dumb.
explanation.definitionFit: Alalia is a medical term for loss or absence of the ability to speak.

clue.text: Fair component of some resins, not mine

indicators.note: not marks the following word as excluded from the longer one

blocks.note: melamine is used to make synthetic resins
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fair share of some resins is claimed by someone else, not me.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun: a festival or market.
explanation.definitionFit: A mela is a Hindu festival or large gathering in South Asia, much like a fair.

clue.text: Ikon crafted with silence by number in shared meal? It's typical of cloistered community

indicators.note: crafted means shaped anew, so the word before is rearranged
in puts the preceding group inside the following word

blocks.note: a mess is a communal meal, as in the services
taken as written
sh is a call for silence
N is a symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: A religious icon is made in silence during a communal meal, as is the way in a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: Monkishness is the quality of being like a monk, characteristic of an enclosed religious order.

clue.text: Fruity cluster eater demolished with joyous cry

indicators.note: a demolished thing is broken up, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
io is a classical cry of joy or triumph

explanation.surface: A greedy eater devours a bunch of fruit with a whoop of delight.
explanation.definitionFit: An etaerio is the botanical name for an aggregate fruit such as a raspberry, a cluster of small fruitlets.

clue.text: Chant involving consecutive trio like wind among the leaves?

indicators.note: involving means wrapping something up within, so the first word surrounds the second

blocks.note: to chant is to sing
three letters next to each other in the alphabet

explanation.surface: A chant takes in a group of three, sounding like a breeze through the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The trio is any run of three alphabet letters; the answer picks which one.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind passing through foliage makes a soft moaning sound, which poets call sighing.

clue.text: Work in bank, say, gets captain confused

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled up and so rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A bank job leaves the boss bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests finance, but it is a peat bank, a bog face from which turves are cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat-casting is the cutting of peat from a bank for fuel, labour done at a bank of earth.

clue.text: Fashionable number turned up in this cut?

indicators.note: turned up in a down entry means read from bottom to top
in puts the reversed piece inside the other
cut as a pack of cards is cut, the letters are shuffled

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
taken as written

explanation.surface: A stylish number turns up wearing this cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' and 'cut' suggest a dress and its tailoring; both are mechanics here.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonish derives from ton, meaning high fashion, so it describes something stylish or modish.

clue.text: A wee bittie whiskey imbibed by soak?

indicators.note: something imbibed is taken inside, so the letter goes within

blocks.note: to sop is to soak
Whiskey is the NATO alphabet word for W

explanation.surface: A little drop of whisky is downed by a drunkard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' tempts as a noun for a drinker, but it is the verb. Wee and bittie are Scots for small and little bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sowp is a Scots form of sup, meaning a small mouthful of liquid, a tiny portion.

clue.text: Duck portion? It may deceive the eye (5, two words)

blocks.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, shaped like O
a part is a portion

explanation.surface: A helping of duck might not be what it looks like.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is an abstract art movement using optical illusions to trick the viewer's perception.

clue.text: Drunk, having imbibed gallon, sky high?

indicators.note: imbibed means taken in, so the letter is placed inside

blocks.note: winy means drunk on wine
G is the abbreviation for gallon

explanation.surface: A drunk who has downed a gallon is as high as a kite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High' suggests intoxication, but it means aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: Wingy means having wings or soaring, so it describes something flying up in the air.

clue.text: An old field having parts switched for hunt?

indicators.note: switching parts means its front and back sections change places

blocks.note: taken as written
glebe is an old word for land or a field

explanation.surface: An ancient meadow is rearranged in preparation for a hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'parts' are not syllables of the field word alone: the article joins the front section, and the last two letters form the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To beagle is to hunt hares on foot with beagles, the small hounds bred for it.

clue.text: Subject I sat in e.g. poly, missing pass at first

indicators.note: a sitter in a place is inside it, so one letter goes within
missing means lacking, so letters are taken away
at first says the letters go from the very front of the longer word

blocks.note: taken as written
a poly, or polytechnic, is an example of a college
a col is a mountain pass

explanation.surface: A subject recalls sitting at the polytechnic, having failed to get through at the first try.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At first' tells you where the pass is removed from: the front of the college.
explanation.definitionFit: A liege is a vassal owing allegiance, so the word means a feudal subject as well as a lord.

clue.text: Mountain plant, strangely pleasing, one picked out

indicators.note: something done strangely is out of the usual order, so letters are rearranged
picked out means removed, so the letter is extracted

blocks.note: taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: An alpine flower is oddly attractive, and one is chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Spignel, or baldmoney, is a fragrant umbelliferous herb that grows in mountain grassland.

clue.text: Painful swelling making one miss work in career

indicators.note: to miss something is to leave it out

blocks.note: to career is to gallop at full speed
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A sore lump forces someone to take time off from their profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a profession, but it is the verb meaning rush along.
explanation.definitionFit: A gall is a sore or swelling, especially one chafed on a horse's skin.

clue.text: Scots engineer, no longer vigorous in energy

blocks.note: rank once meant vigorous or strong in growth
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A Scottish engineer is past his prime and short on energy.
explanation.walkthrough: W J M Rankine was a 19th-century Glasgow engineer and physicist, known for thermodynamics.
explanation.definitionFit: Rankine pioneered thermodynamics, and an absolute temperature scale is named after this Scottish engineer.

clue.text: One born in spring period, English, with rain swirling around

indicators.note: swirling letters are churned about, so they are rearranged
around puts the jumbled word on either side of the letter

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A springtime baby arrives amid swirling English showers.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arien is someone born under Aries, the zodiac sign covering late March to April, in spring.

clue.text: Butterfly? It's thrown out in air gusts

indicators.note: thrown letters are tossed about and land rearranged
out means removed from the rest

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A butterfly is tossed about in gusty winds.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus the letters of the first word together rearrange to the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Argus is the name of several butterflies with eye-spots on the wings, so it is one kind of butterfly.

clue.text: Heather may be so wrinkled around onset of greying

indicators.note: around places the first word on both sides of the letter
the onset of something is its beginning, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: liny means full of lines, wrinkled
only the first letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone named Heather may be wrinkled as she starts to go grey.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant: ling is another name for heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingy means abounding in ling, so heathland covered in heather could be described this way.

clue.text: Student of religious stuff hereto revised, taking in record of work done

indicators.note: a revised text has been reworked, so its letters are rearranged
taking in means accepting inside, so the jumble encloses the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a log is a written record, such as of work carried out

explanation.surface: A divinity scholar revises his work so far, keeping notes of what is done.
explanation.definitionFit: A theologer is an old word for a theologian, someone who studies religion and divinity.
